title: Salt beef and salt pork at sea
h1: Salt beef and salt pork at sea: what the records show, and what salt never promised
dek: Contracts, ration tables and sailors' journals show how navies fed crews on barrelled meat for months. They also show what salt could not do, and why none of it is a recipe for your kitchen.
description: What contracts and journals show about salt beef and pork on sailing warships, where the method failed, and why it is not a modern food-safety model.
recheck: If any listed source changes, or when the primary contracts and journals cited in the museum study are pulled and read directly (see the Limits section).

safety_review.scope: Approved as drafted, no changes requested, including the 'Not validated for modern household use' verdict and the absence of any curing quantities. Approval recorded from the reviewer's one-word reply in chat; item-by-item checklist notes were not supplied. Primary records cited by the museum study remain unpulled.

source_use.usscm-brenckle-2019: 1813 load-out and weekly ration table; the 1812 Binney beef and pork specification; steeping practice; Melville and other journal accounts; bread contract and biscuit dimensions; pests; scurvy theory about 'slush'; 1802 water rules.
source_use.rmg-life-at-sea: Overview of the main shipboard rations, the way storage and vermin degraded food, and the cause of scurvy.
source_use.rmg-biscuit-aab0766: A surviving ship's biscuit in a museum collection, as a physical record of the bread half of the ration.
source_use.si-nmah-life-aboard: A fishing schooner's 1879 provisions list, as a contrast with naval scale.
source_use.si-lind-1753: The digitized 1753 Treatise of the Scurvy, as the primary source for the scurvy discussion.
source_use.jll-trohler-2003: Scholarly account of Lind's trial and the Navy's slow response.
source_use.fsis-botulism: Botulism, the role of nitrite in cured meat, and the link to traditionally prepared salted foods.
source_use.cdc-botulism-prevention: Current botulism prevention advice: pressure canning for low-acid foods, toxin cannot be seen, smelled or tasted.
source_use.fsis-home-cure-qa: USDA's statement that botulism cases have followed home-cured, smoked, preserved and fermented foods.
source_use.nchfp-cure-smoke: Where to find tested home curing and smoking methods, and how the NCHFP describes what curing does.
